Description: SWE-bench Verified evaluates real-world software engineering by asking models to generate patches that fix issues in existing GitHub repositories, validated by running the project’s test suite. The “Verified” subset consists of tasks that have been human-checked to be solvable and to have reliable evaluation signals, making it a common reference for agentic coding performance.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Decision-making
L3:

Description: SWE-bench Multilingual extends SWE-bench-style bug-fixing to multiple programming languages beyond Python, emphasizing generalizable software engineering skill. Models must read problem statements, understand unfamiliar codebases, and produce correct patches that satisfy tests across diverse language ecosystems.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: SWE-bench Pro is a harder, more contamination-resistant software engineering benchmark designed to better reflect industrially relevant tasks across multiple languages and repositories. It emphasizes robust debugging, larger search spaces, and higher difficulty than SWE-bench Verified while still using executable checks to score solutions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Decision-making
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: Terminal-Bench 2.0 evaluates agents operating in a command-line environment on realistic multi-step tasks such as installing tools, manipulating files, running programs, and diagnosing failures. Success depends on correctly sequencing shell actions under constraints and recovering from errors using tool feedback.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility, Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: BrowseComp measures web-browsing research ability: agents must find and synthesize information from web sources to answer questions that typically require multi-hop retrieval and verification. It stresses long-horizon search strategy, source triangulation, and faithful citation/grounding under time and context limits.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Attention, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Decision-making
L3:

Description: τ2-bench evaluates interactive agent performance in multi-turn, policy-constrained customer support settings (e.g., retail, airline, telecom) with tool/API use. Agents must follow domain policies, ask clarifying questions, and coordinate actions across a conversation to resolve user needs without violating constraints.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension, Language Production
L2: Planning, Decision-making
L3: Social Reasoning & Theory of Mind, Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: OSWorld benchmarks computer-use agents in an OS-like graphical environment, requiring navigation, form filling, file operations, and application control from pixel/GUI observations. It tests whether an agent can interpret screen state and execute correct multi-step actions to complete tasks end-to-end.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: ARC-AGI-2 is a few-shot, grid-based abstract reasoning benchmark where models infer hidden transformation rules from a handful of input–output examples and apply them to new inputs. It is intended to measure fluid reasoning and generalization to novel patterns rather than memorized knowledge.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception (minor)
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Spatial Representation & Mapping
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: Vending-Bench 2 evaluates long-horizon autonomous agent coherence and strategy in a simulated business management setting (running a vending machine operation over extended time). Agents must plan inventory, pricing, supplier interactions, and budgeting to maximize final balance while adapting to changing conditions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Reward Mechanisms (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility, Social Reasoning & Theory of Mind (minor)

Description: MCP-Atlas measures tool-use via the Model Context Protocol (MCP): models discover available tools, invoke them correctly, handle errors, and compose multi-step workflows across services. The benchmark emphasizes reliable action selection and integration of tool outputs into correct final responses.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: FinanceAgent evaluates agentic performance on tasks typical of an entry-level financial analyst, such as reading financial documents, performing calculations, and producing structured deliverables (e.g., analyses or spreadsheets). It stresses numerical reasoning, domain knowledge, and multi-step work product creation.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Decision-making, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: CyberGym evaluates cybersecurity agents on tasks involving identifying known vulnerabilities in real open-source projects from descriptions and, in some settings, discovering new vulnerabilities. It stresses code understanding, hypothesis-driven investigation, and producing correct exploit-relevant findings or patches under evaluation harnesses.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)
L3:

Description: SpreadsheetBench tests an agent’s ability to navigate and manipulate complex spreadsheets to solve realistic tasks (e.g., cleaning, transformation, formula editing, and report generation). It emphasizes structured reasoning over tabular data and correct execution of multi-step editing operations.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Working Memory, Decision-making, Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: Humanity’s Last Exam is a large, difficult benchmark spanning frontier academic and professional questions, often requiring deep reasoning and, in some settings, multimodal understanding. It is designed to probe broad expert-level knowledge and the ability to synthesize across complex problem statements.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor), Visual Perception (minor)
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory

Description: AIME 2025 consists of competition mathematics problems that require multi-step derivations and precise final answers. It probes mathematical problem solving under tight correctness requirements and often benefits from systematic intermediate reasoning.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning (minor)
L3:

Description: GPQA Diamond is a high-quality subset of graduate-level science multiple-choice questions designed to be resistant to superficial web search (“Google-proof”). It probes deep scientific knowledge and careful reasoning through tricky distractors and multi-step inference.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory (minor), Decision-making (minor)
L3:

Description: MMMLU extends MMLU to multiple languages, testing broad academic knowledge and reasoning across many subjects in non-English settings. It evaluates whether models can maintain performance when questions, concepts, and phrasing appear in diverse linguistic forms.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: MMMU is a multimodal benchmark where models answer questions requiring combined understanding of images and text across many disciplines. It stresses visual interpretation, cross-referencing textual context, and multi-step reasoning grounded in visual evidence.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Multisensory Integration, Logical Reasoning, Visual Attention & Eye Movements (minor)

Description: MMMU-Pro is a more challenging variant of MMMU designed to better separate top multimodal models, often using harder questions and evaluation settings. It emphasizes robust visual grounding and complex reasoning that integrates information from diagrams, charts, and accompanying text.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Multisensory Integration, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: LAB-Bench FigQA tests whether models can correctly interpret complex scientific figures from biology papers and answer questions that depend on the visual evidence. It probes fine-grained chart/figure reading, integrating domain context, and avoiding hallucinated claims not supported by the figure.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: WebArena evaluates autonomous web agents on realistic tasks across multiple web apps (e-commerce, forums, code hosting, CMS) in a controlled environment. Agents must navigate pages, fill forms, and execute multi-step workflows, often requiring error recovery and long-horizon task management.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception (minor)
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Visual Attention & Eye Movements (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: MathArena Apex is a curated set of difficult mathematics problems intended to benchmark advanced reasoning beyond standard contest sets. It emphasizes multi-step solution construction, precise symbolic manipulation, and robustness across problem types and difficulty levels.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning (minor)
L3:

Description: ScreenShot-Pro evaluates understanding of high-resolution screenshots from software interfaces, dashboards, and professional tools, often requiring spatial and UI-specific reasoning. It probes whether models can correctly ground answers in visual layout and interface elements rather than relying on priors.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor), Planning (minor)
L3:

Description: CharXiv Reasoning tests figure- and chart-based reasoning over scientific paper visuals, typically requiring extraction of quantitative or relational information from plots and diagrams. It emphasizes careful visual grounding and multi-step inference, often benefiting from tool-like computation for numerical accuracy.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Attention (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: OmniDocBench 1.5 evaluates document understanding and OCR across heterogeneous content such as text, formulas, tables, and reading order. It measures how accurately models can extract and structure information from complex page layouts, not just recognize characters.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception, Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Working Memory (minor)

Description: Video-MMMU extends multimodal understanding to video, requiring models to answer questions that depend on events unfolding over time as well as visual details within frames. It probes temporal integration of information, cross-modal reasoning with text prompts, and memory for earlier scene content.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Multisensory Integration, Working Memory, Attention
L3: Cognitive Timing & Predictive Modeling (minor)

Description: LiveCodeBench Pro evaluates competitive coding and practical programming performance on a curated, time-aware set of coding problems, often reported with aggregate metrics such as Elo. It stresses correct algorithm selection, implementation accuracy, and robustness under single-attempt evaluation settings.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning, Decision-making (minor)
L3:

Description: The FACTS Benchmark Suite systematically evaluates LLM factuality across multiple settings (e.g., grounded generation, attribution, and factual consistency), aiming to detect hallucinations and unsupported claims. It emphasizes whether models can stay faithful to sources and separate known facts from speculation.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Working Memory (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control, Self-reflection (minor)

Description: SimpleQA Verified is a factual question answering benchmark with verified ground truth and evaluation designed to reduce ambiguity and contamination. It targets reliability on short, direct factual questions and penalizes confident but incorrect responses.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition
L3: Inhibitory Control

Description: Global PIQA evaluates physical commonsense reasoning across many languages and cultures, often using non-parallel multilingual formulations to test robustness. It probes whether models can select plausible actions or explanations in everyday physical situations under linguistic variation.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning (minor)
L3:

Description: MRCR v2 is a long-context multi-round coreference/recall benchmark where multiple similar “needle” interactions are inserted into long “haystacks,” and the model must retrieve the correct referenced response. The 8-needle variant stresses tracking and discriminating among multiple near-duplicate items across extended context lengths.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Working Memory, Attention, Episodic Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: GDPval evaluates economically valuable, well-specified professional knowledge work across many occupations by scoring real work products (e.g., presentations, spreadsheets, plans) against expert human judgments. It emphasizes end-to-end execution quality, adherence to constraints, and producing usable artifacts rather than only answering questions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Production
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: SWE-Lancer evaluates software engineering in settings closer to real engineering workflows, emphasizing agentic execution and reliability on practical tasks beyond isolated coding puzzles. It is designed to reflect end-to-end problem solving over repositories and task specifications, often with stronger realism constraints than classic coding benchmarks.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: Graphwalks tests long-context algorithmic reasoning over graph-structured data described in text, requiring models to follow traversal or parent/neighbor relations and return correct nodes or paths. It stresses systematic step-by-step tracking of state across many hops and resistance to distraction from irrelevant edges.
Cognitive Functions:
L1:

Description: Toolathon evaluates tool-augmented agents on complex tasks that require selecting among many tools, correctly calling them, and composing outputs into a coherent solution. It emphasizes robust orchestration across heterogeneous APIs and the ability to recover when intermediate tool calls fail or return unexpected data.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility, Self-reflection (minor)

Description: HMMT problems (as packaged in modern evaluation suites) draw from high-school mathematics tournament questions that often require creative multi-step reasoning and careful case handling. It is used to measure progress on advanced quantitative reasoning, frequently with tool support (e.g., Python) to reduce arithmetic errors while preserving core reasoning difficulty.
